column1: # docs/port/tests.tsv lists the tests under tests/ that reach inside the code, and what the port does with each.
# Drawn on 2026-11-20 at main 42239208. The marks and the go_check owners are proposals until the user agrees them (story port-tests-agree).
# tests/port_tests_list_test.sh applies the rule below to every tests/*_test.sh and fails on a test it finds with no row here.
# Columns, tab-separated: file, reach, mark, go_check, epic.
# reach: each way the test reaches inside, comma-separated. Comment lines don't count.
#   lib: it sources a bin/lib/*.sh, itself or through a helper under tests/ (tests/merge_fixture.sh sources agents.sh in a bash -c).
#   py: it names a bin/lib/*.py file, or imports a module of that name.

#   text: it reads a file under bin/ or hooks/ as text: grep, sed, awk, cat, head, tail, wc, perl, diff, cmp, cut, open(), a < redirect or a python3 -c program on the path, a loop over such paths, or git ls-files or os.walk over bin/ or hooks/.
#   Reading hooks/hooks.json is no reach, since it is the plugin's config and the port keeps it.
#   python3-stub: it writes, copies or links a file to a path ending in /python3, a stub to put first on PATH.
#   A test also has every reach of a helper under tests/ that it names.
#   rewrite-from-outside: the bash test stays, and the port that deletes what it reaches rewrites that part to drive the command from outside. A text scanner keeps scanning whatever bash is left.
#   becomes-a-Go-test: its cases move into a Go test of the package, and the bash file goes. Only a few do (HLD:97-98).

# go_check, on every text row (its reach says text, or the test reads the code as text by the rule): what the Go check asserts that keeps the test's rule once the bash it reads is gone. Where the rule's subject goes away with a port, because no such site can exist in Go, it says retired-with: <epic>. It is empty on a row with no text reach.

# epic: on a text row, the epic that adds the go_check. On any other row, the first port epic in stage order that deletes code the test reaches: a helper it names, a function it calls, or a command it runs.
# A new test that reaches inside gets its row in the same PR. A row stays when its test stops reaching or does not exist yet, because the list is the record.
# agreed by the user on 2026-11-20: every mark and owner as proposed (story port-tests-agree).
